title: DPsurv: Dual-Prototype Evidential Fusion for Uncertainty-Aware and Interpretable Whole Slide Image Survival Prediction
claim: A three-stage pipeline turns slides into prototype-based component evidence and fuses it into an uncertainty-aware survival curve.
layout: 3 colored stage banners, left-to-right, dashed zoom-in boxes with math
description: A wide, dense diagram under three gradient banners: Deep Slide Component Embedding (purple), Component Evidence Modeling (pink), and Component Evidence Mixture (orange). On the left, a whole-slide image is patched, passed through a frozen encoder into a feature set, and clustered by a GMM into colored patch prototypes. In the middle, a dashed box shows three example slides as Prototype₁–₃ with similarity scores (s₁–s₃), evidence curves (μ, σ², h), and GRFN modules. Below it, the slide embedding (π, μ, Σ) goes through evidential mapping to component evidence. On the right, a dashed box shows component-specific Gaussian curves that are weighted by π and combined into a multimodal density. The flow ends at a predicted survival curve with dashed blue and orange bounds. Pink, purple and orange color-code the components, and red arrows mark the weighting path.
caption: Overview of the DPsurv framework Deep Slide Component Embedding encodes WSI into deep feature embeddings with patch prototypes; Component Evidence Modeling maps deep embeddings into evidence through component prototypes, and Component Evidence Mixture aggregates component evidence into transformed survival functions, illustrated by the Plausibility (blue dashed line) and Belief (orange dashed line) survival curves.
abstract: Pathology whole-slide images (WSIs) are widely used for cancer survival analysis because of their comprehensive histopathological information at both cellular and tissue levels, enabling quantitative, large-scale, and prognostically rich tumor feature analysis. However, most existing methods in WSI survival analysis struggle with limited interpretability and often overlook predictive uncertainty in heterogeneous slide images. In this paper, we propose DPsurv, a dual-prototype whole-slide image evidential fusion network that outputs uncertainty-aware survival intervals, while enabling interpretation of predictions through patch prototype assignment maps, component prototypes, and component-wise relative risk aggregation. Experiments on five publicly available datasets achieve the highest mean concordance index and the lowest mean integrated Brier score, validating the effectiveness and reliability of DPsurv. The interpretation of prediction results provides transparency at the feature, reasoning, and decision levels, thereby enhancing the trustworthiness and interpretability of DPsurv.
